name: Red Vein Aglaonema
description: Aglaonema rotundum is a compact aroid in the Araceae family, native to tropical Asia (Sumatra, New Guinea). It has rounded to oval leaves with striking pink or red veins and pink undersides, making it a sought-after ornamental. It tolerates low to medium light and prefers well-draining, aerated soil; overwatering leads to root rot. Like other Aglaonema, it contains calcium oxalate crystals and is toxic if ingested. It suits terrariums and vivariums with moderate humidity and warm temperatures.
careTips: Low to bright indirect light; avoid direct sun which can scorch leaves
Allow the top 2–3 cm of soil to dry between waterings; well-draining mix essential
Use aerated potting mix with perlite, vermiculite, or coco coir
Moderate humidity (50–60%) is appreciated; adapts to average indoor humidity
Repot when the plant outgrows its container; fresh soil helps avoid over-fertilizing
Toxic if ingested—keep away from pets and children
